_source: ChirpStack device link-metrics, 31d view (DAY aggregation), retrieved 2026-08-19 by temporarily shifting the page clock so the fixed 31d range covered historical months. Page clock restored afterwards.
_retention_finding: Daily aggregates are retained ~61 days. On 2026-08-19 the earliest available daily bucket was 2026-06-19. Months before that are available only at MONTH aggregation. July 2026 daily sums to 140 for SENZOR_03, exactly matching its monthly figure, which validates the retrieval method.
_label_caveat: Bucket timestamps appear to be local-midnight aligned (UTC+2); labels below are ISO/UTC slices, so a late-evening local event can appear on the following UTC date. This is why SENZOR_02 shows a frame on 06-24 despite a last-seen of 2026-06-23 21:42 local.
_sample_size_caveat: Daily mean RSSI/SNR are computed over 1-12 frames. With so few frames the daily mean is noisy, and spread is driven mainly by frame count. See the control below.
_conclusion_supported: The cliff is sharp at DAILY resolution. SENZOR_04 transmitted 5 frames on its final day against an annual mean of 4.9/day, with no ramp-down over its last six days. Same for SENZOR_02. Cessation is abrupt, not a fade.
_conclusion_NOT_supported: There is NO usable pre-death link-quality signature. The dying units show RSSI spreads of 8.4 and 15.7 dB over their final days, but surviving SENZOR_05 shows 10.7 dB over the same days. Spread tracks frame count, not device health: SENZOR_03 with 2-12 frames/day spreads 3.8 dB while SENZOR_05 with 1-3 frames/day spreads 10.7 dB. SENZOR_04's apparent monotone decay over its last two days (-102.6, -107.3, -109.4) is within what small-sample noise produces on a healthy device, and SENZOR_02 shows no comparable trend. Do not claim a pre-failure RSSI signature.

july_2026_validation.note: exact match; validates the clock-shift retrieval method
